patient.chief_complaint: Shuffling gait with falls, urinary incontinence, and progressive memory loss over 2.5 years — family requested evaluation
patient.history_present_illness: A 77-year-old retired interior designer with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (on apixaban), hypertension, and hyperlipidemia was admitted for NPH evaluation. Her son and daughter-in-law prompted the admission after recognizing the classic NPH triad from an article they read. She has had progressive gait difficulty over the past 2.5 years, starting with an insidious change in step length and gait speed. She now has a distinctive wide-based shuffling walk and has had six falls in the past 18 months — including one serious fall that required emergency department evaluation for possible hip fracture (X-rays negative). She now uses a cane indoors and a rollator walker outdoors. Her urinary urgency began approximately 20 months ago, progressing from urgency without leakage to daily leakage. She rarely leaves home without wearing protective undergarments. Her cognitive decline has been notable: she can no longer manage her finances (her son has taken over), she repeats questions frequently within the same conversation, and she has twice gotten confused while walking in her own apartment building. She has been taking apixaban for 14 months for paroxysmal AF diagnosed after a Holter monitor. The anticoagulation will need to be held before lumbar puncture. Neuroimaging obtained two months ago shows markedly enlarged ventricles. She was admitted for comprehensive NPH workup including DOAC hold protocol before LP.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented to person and place; cannot state the date. MoCA 20/30. Impaired delayed recall (1/5), executive dysfunction, poor serial subtraction. No aphasia. Mildly reduced insight.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Normal. No papilledema. Extraocular movements intact.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal tone and strength. No rigidity. No resting tremor.
neurological_exam.sensory: Mild symmetric vibration loss at ankles. Light touch intact.
neurological_exam.gait: Wide-based, severely magnetic gait. Short steps. Freezing at doorways. TUG 30 seconds. 10-meter walk 24 seconds. Cannot tandem walk. Pull test — 3 steps backward.
neurological_exam.additional: Bilateral grasp reflexes. Snout reflex positive. No nuchal rigidity. Irregular rhythm noted — heart rate 72 bpm, irregular.

mri.impression: Diagnostic iNPH findings: Evans index 0.39, callosal angle 74°, DESH, periventricular transependymal signal, hyperdynamic aqueductal flow void. Mild to moderate white matter changes from atrial fibrillation and hypertension. Clinical correlation recommended.

Coagulation.value: Held 48h prior to LP — DOAC hold protocol followed

abnormal_values_summary: Apixaban held per DOAC protocol — not an abnormal value but important for LP safety

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 14 cmH2O. WBC: 2 cells/mcL (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 43 mg/dL. Glucose: 69 mg/dL (ratio 0.72). cytology: No malignant cells. beta_amyloid_42: 748 pg/mL (normal). total_tau: 202 pg/mL (normal). phospho_tau: 22 pg/mL (normal).

specialized_test.test_type: High-volume tap trial (40 mL) with quantitative gait analysis

findings.urinary: Decreased urgency at 24h; no incontinence episode

specialized_test.impression: Positive tap trial. TUG improved 33% at 24 hours (30 sec to 20 sec); 10-meter walk improved 33% (24 sec to 16 sec); MoCA improved 3 points (20 to 23). Decreased urgency and no incontinence episode at 24 hours. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.proposed: VP shunt surgery in patient on apixaban (CHADS2-VASc 3) for paroxysmal AF
interactions: Apixaban must be held 48-72h before neurosurgical procedure
warnings: CHADS2-VASc 3 — moderate stroke risk during apixaban hold; discuss bridging anticoagulation with neurosurgery and cardiology (parenteral anticoagulation if high thrombotic risk)
Resume apixaban 48-72h post-operatively once hemostasis confirmed
Do not hold apixaban without a clear anticoagulation management plan
alternatives: Warfarin (subtherapeutic INR window perioperatively) — not preferred vs DOAC

output.impression: Negative — sparse-to-no amyloid neuritic plaque density. CL score 12, below the threshold of 24. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings: Predominantly sinus rhythm with three episodes of paroxysmal AF (3-8 minutes each, self-terminating). Rate well-controlled on metoprolol.
output.impression: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation confirmed. Three episodes recorded over 24 hours (3–8 minutes each, self-terminating); AF burden 4% of total recording. Ventricular rate well-controlled throughout. Sinus rhythm predominates. Clinical correlation recommended.

Hyperdynamic aqueductal flow. Peak velocity 22 cm/s (reference <18 cm/s); stroke volume 80 mcL/cycle (reference <42 mcL/cycle). Both values exceed published normative ranges. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.query: atrial fibrillation cardioembolic dementia differentiation from NPH white matter

results.title: AF-associated dementia vs iNPH — clinical and imaging differentiation
results.key_finding: AF increases vascular dementia risk via cardioembolic microinfarcts; however positive tap trial with NPH imaging strongly supports iNPH as primary treatable diagnosis regardless of AF history

output.summary: Atrial fibrillation increases vascular dementia risk via cardioembolic microinfarcts. In patients with concurrent AF and NPH imaging features, a positive tap trial (TUG >20%) is associated with iNPH as the dominant process. White matter hyperintensities associated with AF and hypertension may coexist with iNPH. Clinical correlation is required.

findings.finding: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity — involuntary contractions at 130 mL. No outlet obstruction.

output.impression: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity. Involuntary contractions at 130 mL. No outlet obstruction. Pattern is consistent with detrusor overactivity of neurogenic origin. Clinical correlation recommended.

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.
Trace mitral regurgitation, physiological. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.
echo.impression: Structurally near-normal heart with a benign incidental finding.

differential.diagnosis: Cardioembolic dementia / vascular dementia from atrial fibrillation
differential.key_features: No cortical or subcortical infarcts on MRI; mild WMH only. Positive tap trial and NPH imaging confirm iNPH as primary diagnosis.
Normal CSF biomarkers; negative amyloid PET (CL 12) despite mother with AD. Frontal-subcortical cognitive pattern.
Mild WMH (Fazekas 1-2); positive tap trial confirms NPH dominance
Classic Hakim's triad, diagnostic imaging, strongly positive tap trial

key_reasoning_points: Classic iNPH Hakim's triad — Evans 0.39, callosal angle 74°, DESH, strongly positive tap trial (33%)
DOAC (apixaban) management is a critical safety step for both LP and VP shunt surgery
Paroxysmal AF is a vascular risk factor but not the cause of the NPH syndrome
Family history of AD with negative amyloid PET confirms NPH-only etiology
CHADS2-VASc 3 requires careful perioperative anticoagulation plan for shunt surgery

red_herrings.intended_effect: Family history of Alzheimer's combined with significant cognitive impairment may prompt AD diagnosis and defer NPH workup
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Negative amyloid PET (CL 12) and normal CSF biomarkers exclude Alzheimer's disease. NPH is the primary treatable diagnosis.

red_herrings.data_point: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with mild white matter changes on MRI
red_herrings.intended_effect: White matter changes combined with AF history may lead to vascular dementia diagnosis, deferring NPH evaluation
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: No infarcts on MRI. DESH pattern, Evans 0.39, callosal angle 74°, and strongly positive tap trial confirm iNPH. White matter changes are coincidental.

metadata.difficulty_variant_description: Straightforward iNPH in a 77-year-old retired designer on apixaban for paroxysmal AF — classic triad, florid MRI, strongly positive tap trial. DOAC management as critical safety consideration. AF/WMH and family history of AD as red herrings.
